attacks.claim: The locker vendor receives card scans and card-number+PIN entries for every pickup, but the artifact names no data processing terms for it and no retention for its card-read or pickup logs. Only the SMS provider is covered by a DPA.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: DPA or data processing terms for the locker vendor and retention for locker access logs. Artifact says only '3 locker banks (48 cells each) installed and acceptance-tested by the vendor'.

attacks.claim: Card number plus PIN is accepted on an unattended 24/7 public touchscreen, and the artifact describes no shoulder-surfing protection, keypad tamper or skimmer detection, or camera coverage.
attacks.evidence: 'or enters card number + PIN, existing ILS PIN lockout applies'; ABSENT: anti-shoulder-surfing, tamper detection, or CCTV for the locker kiosks.

attacks.claim: Confirmed numbers have no reassignment handling. A patron who gives up a number keeps sending hold texts, including branch, hold count and pickup code, to whoever holds that number next. The 72-hour purge covers only unconfirmed numbers.
attacks.evidence: 'Unconfirmed numbers are deleted after 72 h.' ABSENT: handling for confirmed numbers later reassigned, or any re-verification or stale-number check.

attacks.claim: STOP handling depends solely on the provider and our webhook reaching us. There is no retry, queue or reconciliation for missed STOP events, and monitoring alerts only on signature failures, so an opt-out could go unrecorded locally.
attacks.evidence: 'STOP ... is honored by the provider and our signed webhook, which clears the opt-in flag.' Monitoring: 'webhook signature failures > 0'; ABSENT: retry, reconciliation, or alert for lost STOP events.

attacks.claim: Juvenile-related hold information, including counts, branch and pickup codes, is sent by text to a guardian's own phone. The artifact does not show this was analysed against state library-records confidentiality rules for minors.
attacks.evidence: 'guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account'; ABSENT: minors' library-record confidentiality analysis, or any mention of it in LGL-118.

attacks.claim: The $900/month production hard cap and 70% ops alert are asserted but never verified on the production account. The only cap test used a $5 test cap on a test-mode provider account, so the cost-protection and no-alert-lost claims are unproven at production settings.
attacks.evidence: 'Spend cap reached (test cap $5) → fallback to email / phone call | Pass' and 'Provider account hard spend cap $900/month, alert to ops at 70%'. ABSENT: evidence the production cap and alert are set and verified.

attacks.claim: The spend-cap and outage fallback to email or phone is not monitored for delivery success, so patrons who only had SMS or whose fallback fails could silently miss holds. The delivery-failure alert also would not fire on a total provider outage that returns no status callbacks, and queue depth and SMS-to-fallback switching have no alert.
attacks.evidence: 'Dashboard: texts sent, delivery rate, STOP rate, queue depth, locker cell status. Alerts: delivery failures > 5% for 15 min, webhook signature failures > 0, any locker bank offline > 10 min'; ABSENT: fallback-delivery monitor, queue-depth alert, or outage-without-callbacks detection.

attacks.claim: Full-base launch is set for all cardholders at 09:00 on the production send path with no staged ramp. The staff pilot of 64 cards does not exercise production volume or the announcement-driven opt-in surge.
attacks.evidence: '2. Nov 9 09:00: flags on for all cardholders; announcement goes out at 10:00 only after a smoke test of one live text and one locker pickup per branch.'

attacks.claim: The locker rollback remaps pickup_location and asks staff to move items, but it does not say whether already-issued codes stop opening cells. The 1,200-row staging test does not show production row counts or the ILS write path at launch volume, and there is no stated upper bound on locked items across 144 cells.
attacks.evidence: '`locker_pickup` off: holds currently assigned to a locker ... are remapped ... (tested in staging on 1,200 rows), staff move items to the holds shelf'; ABSENT: code invalidation step, production row count, and item-count bound.

attacks.claim: Flag-off rollback sends patrons back to their previous channel, but QA only tests the spend-cap fallback. There is no evidence the fallback works for patrons with no email, phone-only patrons, or patrons with an unreachable prior channel.
attacks.evidence: 'every opted-in patron gets hold notices by their previous method (email or automated phone call, kept on file).' QA table lists only 'Spend cap reached (test cap $5) → fallback to email / phone call | Pass'.

attacks.claim: Codes expire at the pickup deadline, but the artifact does not say whether a 3-day extension reissues or re-dates the code. A patron may be told a code is valid when the hold has been extended or the code has expired, and reuse after a successful pickup is not addressed.
attacks.evidence: 'Codes are single-use, expire at the pickup deadline' and 'hold is extended 3 days, with a notice on the patron's chosen channel'; ABSENT: code behaviour on extension or reuse.

attacks.claim: Accessibility QA covers only the opt-in web form. The locker touchscreen's audio guidance, high-contrast mode, text-size adjustment and reach-range claims have no test row and rest only on vendor acceptance.
attacks.evidence: 'Touchscreen and card reader mounted within ADA reach range (max 48 in)' and 'Opt-in form with NVDA + Firefox, VoiceOver iOS; 320/768/1280 px layouts | Pass'; ABSENT: locker audio, high-contrast or text-size QA.

attacks.claim: The verbatim announcement says 'every cardholder', but juvenile cards cannot opt in and lockers exist at only three branches. The mandated copy overstates reach and will generate confusion or complaints.
attacks.evidence: 'Text alerts for holds, for every cardholder. 24/7 pickup lockers at Oak Street, Millbrook and Harbor.'

attacks.claim: The consent disclosure is quoted only in English, but the flow runs in Spanish too. The Spanish disclosure text is not shown, so the consent record's language basis is unverified.
attacks.evidence: Disclosure quoted only in English; the flow is stated as 'English and Spanish, following the patron's existing language preference'.

attacks.claim: When the SMS cap is hit, opted-in patrons fall back to automated phone calls to mobile numbers. The artifact does not show that existing call consent covers automated calls to mobile numbers under TCPA.
attacks.evidence: 'every opted-in patron falls back to their previous notice method (email or automated phone call, which stays on file)'; ABSENT: TCPA consent analysis for automated calls to mobile numbers.

attacks.claim: Consent records, including IP address, are kept in the patron record with no stated retention period while the patron remains active. The 30-day purge covers only the notification log.
attacks.evidence: 'consent record (timestamp, IP, checkbox text version) are stored in the patron record'; the 30-day purge applies only to 'The notification log'.

attacks.claim: The single-use pickup code travels in plaintext SMS and can be seen on lock screens or shared phones. The card factor limits the risk, but the artifact does not consider preview or shared-device exposure.
attacks.evidence: 'Code 482913, pick up by Sat Nov 14.' ABSENT: lock-screen preview or shared-device mitigation.

attacks.claim: Locked cells have no defined unlock path outside staffed hours. Lockout alerts go only to branch staff, so a hold could stay stuck until the next staffed visit.
attacks.evidence: '5 wrong attempts lock the cell and alert branch staff'; ABSENT: who unlocks a cell, how fast, and how the patron recovers the hold outside opening hours.

attacks.claim: Queued texts released at 08:00 and the 3-per-day cap are not reconciled. No throttle is specified for the 08:00 release, and it is unclear which day a queued text counts against.
attacks.evidence: 'Texts are sent only 08:00-20:00 patron local time; anything later is queued to 08:00. Max 3 texts per patron per day; extra holds are batched into one message.'

attacks.claim: No load test at full cardholder scale is listed, and no bound is stated for the unconfirmed-number deletion job or notification-log growth at 210k patrons.
attacks.evidence: 'Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts'; ABSENT: full-scale load or deletion-job bounds.

attacks.claim: The 38,000 texts/month forecast and $0.012 per text have no stated derivation or per-patron volume model, so headroom under the $900 cap is unverified.
attacks.evidence: 'Forecast 38,000 texts/month at about $0.012 all-in = ~$460/month'.

attacks.claim: Withdrawal deletes numbers and consent records only in our system. Provider-side deletion, sub-processors and residency are not stated, and 10DLC registration is tied to this one provider.
attacks.evidence: 'If SMS is withdrawn permanently, numbers and consent records are deleted within 30 days and patrons are emailed.'; ABSENT: provider-side deletion commitment or sub-processor list.

attacks.claim: Consent ownership is unspecified when a juvenile card converts to teen at 13. Consent records or phone numbers could stay attached to the guardian or the wrong patron.
attacks.evidence: 'guardians can opt in with their own number on the linked guardian account'; ABSENT: data-model rule for consent ownership on card conversion.

attacks.claim: The pilot's acceptance criteria are not stated as numeric go/no-go thresholds for delivery rate, STOP rate or fallback success, so the all-cardholder decision lacks a defined bar.
attacks.evidence: 'Staff pilot week (64 staff cards, real holds) | 0 misdelivered texts; 2 copy fixes shipped and re-verified'; ABSENT: delivery-rate or STOP-rate go/no-go thresholds.
